items.title: TBM 428: Yes, Robot. Yes, Boss?
items.summary: John Cutler argues that AI in the workplace amplifies whichever direction a team is already heading — genuine collaboration and clarity, or manipulation and avoidance.
items.why: The 'AI amplifies your direction' frame is directly useful for how you introduce AI tools into design and product workflows at Cuemath — the same tool can compound craft or compound noise, depending on how it lands.

items.title: Object-Centric Image Editing in Reve
items.summary: Luke Wroblewski walks through Reve's new image tool where you edit a structured layout of objects instead of typing prompts, so you can grab and change one element at a time.
items.why: This is the shape of the next generation of design tools — object-level control instead of prompt-lottery — and worth tracking as the CueDesign team thinks about which AI workflows to bring in-house.

items.title: 2026 AI and UX Predictions: A Mid-Year Reality Check
items.summary: Jakob Nielsen grades his January AI/UX predictions six months in, calling out where models have raced ahead of usability and which shifts he missed entirely.
items.why: A cheap, high-signal way to recalibrate your own read on where AI-plus-design is actually heading versus the hype — useful before your next planning cycle.

items.title: Building a brand means building a world – Blanca Doba's identity for Bare Earth
items.summary: A designer's identity project for a fictional beauty brand, extending a wordmark into a full whimsical world of calligraphic type, soft palettes, lace borders and archival illustration.
items.why: Exactly the world-building move Cuemath's brand needs when pushing beyond a logo into a system of textures, decorations, and character — good reference for editorial-type-led identity systems with warmth.

items.title: Twofold Therapy
items.summary: Identity and website for a New York psychoanalytic practice that pairs GT America (a crisp modern sans) with GT Super Text (a warm 1970s-style serif) for interface clarity and human tone.
items.why: A clean case study in serif-plus-sans pairing that carries clinical authority and warmth at once — the same tension you're negotiating in kids' learning surfaces where trust and playfulness both have to show up.

items.title: Cord Studio on using symmetry and cinema to create one of 2026's most viral campaigns
items.summary: The Delhi fashion label breaks down its 'Album '91' campaign — symmetrical, cinematic frames staged around 1990s Indian summer-vacation nostalgia — and how a hyper-local memory travelled globally.
items.why: Rare, high-craft case of an Indian brand going worldwide by leaning into cultural specificity, not away from it — useful ammunition next time you're arguing for a distinctly Indian visual direction rather than a generic global one.
